api.pagination: USGS FDSN service imposes a 20000-event hard cap per request (HTTP 400 'exceeds search limit of 20000' returned on the unpaginated query); catalog was retrieved in 2 pages via limit=20000&offset=1 and limit=20000&offset=20001, concatenated, and de-duplicated by USGS event `id` (0 duplicates found, 32688+12688 un-paginated check not applicable -- page1=20000 rows, page2=12688 rows).
api.note_on_discrepancy: The Phase 0.5 search agent reported 30131 events for this same nominal window/box/magnitude description; this run's own independent query against the live USGS FDSN API on 2026-08-15 returned 32688 events for the exact parameters listed above (confirmed via both /count and full /query retrieval, matching row-for-row after dedup). The ~2557-event difference is most plausibly explained by catalog revision over time (magnitudes reviewed/added/removed between the original search and now) and/or a slightly different exact bounding box or endtime used by the original agent -- this was NOT reverse-engineered to match 30131; the number actually returned by the query as specified in the task is what was used and reported here.

mainshock.confirmation_method: Cross-checked two independent ways: (1) present in the bulk /fdsnws/event/1/query CSV catalog itself (row with id=ci38457511, mag=7.1); (2) independently re-fetched via single-event /fdsnws/event/1/query?eventid=ci38457511&format=geojson, which returned identical time=1562383193040 epoch-ms == 2019-07-06T03:19:53.040Z, mag=7.1, title='M 7.1 - Ridgecrest Earthquake Sequence'.

provenance.m6_plus_confounder_note: Two M>=6 events fall inside the 2-month download window: the M6.4 foreshock (ci38443183) on 2019-07-04T17:33:49Z, and the M7.1 mainshock (ci38457511) itself on 2019-07-06T03:19:53.040Z. The M6.4 foreshock is NOT after the mainshock, so per METHODOLOGY_NOTE.md gap (d) it does not require a POST-side cut (no additional M6+ event was found strictly between the mainshock and the end of the download window on 2019-09-04, so POST needed no confounder cut). However, this run flags explicitly that the M6.4's own aftershock sequence occupies essentially the entire PRE window here (PRE primary spans only ~35.06h, from 2019-07-04T16:13:43Z -- ~80 min before the M6.4 -- to the M7.1 origin time), which is why real_pre's fitted event rate (mu_pre) in the PRIMARY variant (0.01444 events/s) is actually HIGHER than real_post's rate averaged over the full 2-month POST window (0.00266 events/s) -- PRE is not a quiescent background segment in this dataset, it is itself dominated by a different mainshock's aftershock decay. This is reported as-is per the fixed METHODOLOGY_NOTE.md rule (no PRE-side cut is specified there, only a POST-side one), not corrected or reformulated.

mc_determination.method: Wiemer & Wyss (2000) maximum-curvature: Mc = center of the 0.1-magnitude bin with the highest event count in the (non-cumulative) frequency-magnitude histogram, computed independently on PRE-mainshock and POST-mainshock event sets (both using the RAW M>=0.5 catalog, before any Mc cut is applied).
mc_determination.note: Mc_POST came out slightly LOWER than Mc_PRE (1.05 vs 1.15), the opposite of the a priori STAI expectation stated in METHODOLOGY_NOTE.md ('Mc_POST provavelmente sera mais alto'). Reported honestly, not adjusted: the maximum-curvature estimate is computed over each segment's FULL span (all ~60 days POST vs ~2 days PRE), so any short-term STAI incompleteness immediately after the mainshock is diluted by the much larger number of later, fully-complete POST days dominating that histogram's peak bin. The prescribed formula (max of the two + 0.2 safety margin) was applied exactly as specified regardless of which segment ended up higher.

transition.rule: PRE = events with mag >= Mc_final, from start of download window (2019-07-04T00:00:00Z) to mainshock origin time (exclusive). POST = events with mag >= Mc_final, from mainshock origin time (inclusive) to end of download window (2019-09-04T00:00:00Z).

pre_robustness_most_recent_50pct_by_coun.definition: Most recent 50% by event COUNT of pre_primary (i.e. the half closest in time to the mainshock).

post_robustness_closest_50pct_by_count.definition: 50% of post_primary closest to the transition by event COUNT (i.e. the earliest half, closest to the mainshock).

segments.event_timestamp_units: Unix epoch seconds (UTC, float, sub-second precision preserved from original catalog timestamps), passed directly as pre_events/post_events to run_soc_pipeline. lambda, duration, and mu in the pipeline output below are therefore all in seconds / events-per-second.
